skill.name: managing-branches
skill.description: Manage Git branching strategies, branch naming, merge flows, and worktree workflows for structured development.
skill.summary: Guides Git branch creation, validation, merging, cleanup, and worktree use across common branching models.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The skill contains legitimate Git automation scripts that execute git subprocesses and can modify branches, worktrees, and local configuration. Most static findings are documentation examples or false positives, but executable worktree and branch management should require user awareness because it changes repository state and filesystem paths.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before checkout, pull, merge, branch deletion, forced worktree removal, or other destructive Git operations.

remediation.issue: Worktree paths may be supplied by users or configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve worktree paths, reject unsafe parent traversal outside an approved base directory, and show the final path before creating or removing files.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes forced worktree removal and global Git ignore examples.
remediation.suggestion: Label these commands as optional and potentially destructive, and prefer project-local configuration examples where possible.

content.value_statement: Branching rules are hard to apply consistently across teams and release models. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for branch naming, flow checks, merges, releases, and worktrees.
actual_capabilities: Explains GitFlow, GitHub Flow, trunk-based, release, and hotfix branch patterns.
Generates branch names from configured prefixes, issue numbers, and naming rules.
Validates branch names and merge targets against local workflow configuration.
Provides scripts for branch start, finish, status, list, cleanup, and configuration tasks.
Provides worktree creation, listing, removal, cleanup, and status workflows.
Includes reference guides and configuration templates for common team branching models.
limitations: It assumes Git is installed and the current directory is inside a Git repository.
Automation changes local repository state and should be reviewed before use.
Remote branch and pull behavior depends on the repository origin and permissions.
It does not replace team review of release, hotfix, or protected branch policies.

use_cases.title: Start feature work safely
use_cases.description: Create a correctly named feature or bugfix branch from the expected base branch.

use_cases.title: Coordinate release and hotfix flows
use_cases.description: Follow merge targets for release branches, hotfix branches, and protected main branches.

use_cases.title: Use worktrees for parallel changes
use_cases.description: Set up separate worktrees for reviews, hotfixes, and feature work without switching one checkout repeatedly.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a branch type
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to work on a small bug fix. Tell me which branch type to use and what branch name to create.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a branch name
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch name against our configured branching rules: feature/issue-123-add-login.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a hotfix flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create and finish a hotfix branch for a production security patch. Include merge targets and checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a team branching strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare GitFlow, GitHub Flow, and trunk-based development for our team. Recommend branch prefixes, merge targets, and worktree rules.

output_examples.input: Start a feature branch for issue 42 named payment retry.
output_examples.output: A branch plan with the feature prefix, issue reference, base branch, update step, and next actions for committing and finishing the branch.

output_examples.input: Can this hotfix merge into main and develop?
output: Identifies the branch as a hotfix.
Warns about required status checks and release tagging.

output_examples.input: Set up a worktree for reviewing pull request 123.
output_examples.output: A worktree plan that names the branch, target path, checkout command, review steps, and cleanup reminder.

best_practices: Review generated Git commands before running them, especially merge, delete, and force options.
Keep branch naming rules in project configuration so all contributors use the same prefixes.
Use worktrees for parallel reviews or hotfixes, then clean them after branches are merged.
anti_patterns: Do not run forced worktree removal when a worktree has uncommitted changes.
Do not bypass protected branch rules by merging directly into main without review.
Do not create ad hoc branch prefixes that are absent from the team configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill create branches automatically?
faq.answer: It can provide scripts and commands for branch creation. Users should review actions before they run.

faq.question: Which branching strategies does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GitFlow, GitHub Flow, trunk-based development, release branches, hotfixes, and worktree patterns.

faq.question: Can it validate branch names?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks prefixes, allowed characters, length, issue rules, and configured branch conventions.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it contact external services?
faq.answer: The reviewed content only showed localhost documentation links. Git operations may contact configured remotes when users run pull or similar commands.

faq.question: What should teams configure first?
faq.answer: Define main and develop branch names, branch prefixes, merge targets, naming rules, and worktree base directories.
